context: Recovering from my own branching mistake on #635: I had committed the workflow changes onto the #592 branch, so I created the correct branch at that commit and then ran mcp__operum__git_reset (hard) to rewind the #592 branch to its pushed head. That reset reverted five files I had edited, and FIVE notices arrived appended to the single git_reset result. A sixth arrived on the following reset to origin/main. Known-benign trigger class: a hard reset rewrites files you had open, exactly as a branch switch does.
verbatim:
Note: /Users/dmitrystepanov/Library/Application Support/.operum/2201f8f0-askturret-mcp/engineer/repo/.github/workflows/test.yml changed on disk since you last read it. That's usually deliberate, so take it as the current state rather than reverting it; if the change looks wrong, say so rather than undoing it yourself — otherwise no need to call it out. Here are the relevant changes (shown with line numbers):
1	name: Test
[ELIDED BY THE CAPTURING AGENT: listing lines 2-154. Prose above is complete and unmodified. The harness rendered line 154, then a BLANK line, then the truncation marker as the FINAL line of the message, transcribed byte-for-byte here: '... [801 lines truncated] ...'.]
factor_1_basis: tool-result-adjacent. The notices followed mcp__operum__git_reset, which returns structured JSON ({"ref":"...","result":"hard reset"}); English prose paragraphs outside that JSON are plainly not payload, so the boundary is legible and the determination is real. Not attributable to any fetch: this reminder text was not read from any file, issue, PR, comment, commit or diff this session.
stated_cause_evidence: Verified from git state, not from the message. The cause was my OWN git_reset --hard, twice: first rewinding the #592 branch to its pushed head fb2a279 after I mistakenly committed #635 work onto it, then resetting the new #635 branch to origin/main to drop the inherited #592 commits. Confirmed by git_log (origin/main..HEAD on #592 shows exactly fb2a279 + 4cc6b0b, matching PR #669's remote head) and by git_status. No external actor touched these files. The message makes no per-instance actor claim beyond the generic 'that's usually deliberate', so there is nothing per-instance to falsify.
emission_note: SIX notices across two git_reset results in one turn, covering at least three variants of the same family: T1C (prose + numbered listing + truncation marker) for test.yml and supply-chain.yml; T1 (prose + untruncated listing) for dco.yml; and T1B (prose + 'The diff is omitted here because other changed files this turn already filled the snippet budget') for lane-check.yml and CONTRIBUTING.md. Recorded as ONE row per EMISSION EVENT, following the precedent of 20260826T005800Z-engineer-331 which captured two notices arriving on a single git_checkout result. template_id names the variant of the transcribed verbatim; the others are recorded here rather than being lost.
factor_2_method: Matched with the repository's own matcher earlier this session (compileTemplate/matchMessage from check-concealment-templates.mjs) against this same allowlist blob, whole-message, with controls: prose-only and prose-plus-arbitrary-tail both NO MATCH, an untruncated listing returns T1 and a truncated one T1C. The templates blob hash was recomputed locally for this row and is unchanged at b6ab2b98.
